record.paper_title: Homogenization in mechanics. A survey of solved and open problems
record.original_question: What boundary-layer corrections arise in homogenized solid-fluid mixture problems under different mechanical boundary conditions, including clamped bodies and bodies with free surfaces?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a periodic solid–fluid mixture occupying a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, modeled by a microstructure of period $\varepsilon$ in which a connected elastic solid phase $\Omega_s^\varepsilon$ and a connected viscous (or inviscid) fluid phase $\Omega_f^\varepsilon$ are arranged $\varepsilon$-periodically. Let $u^\varepsilon$ denote the displacement (in the solid) and velocity/pressure pair (in the fluid) satisfying the coupled linear elasticity / Stokes (or Navier–Stokes) system with the usual continuity of traction and velocity across the solid–fluid interface, together with a prescribed mechanical boundary condition on $\partial\Omega$. Two cases of boundary conditions are to be considered:

(a) the clamped case, where $u^\varepsilon = 0$ on $\partial\Omega$;

(b) the free-surface case, where the normal traction vanishes on $\partial\Omega$.

As $\varepsilon \to 0$, the two-scale asymptotic expansion
$$u^\varepsilon(x) \;=\; u^0(x, x/\varepsilon) \;+\; \varepsilon\, u^1(x, x/\varepsilon) \;+\; \varepsilon^2 u^2(x, x/\varepsilon) \;+\; \cdots$$
formally yields an effective (homogenized) macroscopic system (e.g. Biot-type poroelasticity, viscoelasticity, or Darcy-type behavior, depending on scaling) for the leading term $u^0$. However, the prescribed boundary conditions on $\partial\Omega$ are in general incompatible with the periodic cell profiles, so that boundary-layer correctors—rapidly oscillating functions that decay exponentially away from $\partial\Omega$—must be added to match the data and to obtain optimal-order convergence rates.

Problem. Construct and characterize the boundary-layer correctors that arise in the homogenization of such periodic solid–fluid mixtures in each of the two cases (a) clamped boundary and (b) free-surface boundary. Specifically:

(i) Formulate the cell-like problems on the appropriate half-space (or semi-infinite strip) that define the boundary layers, including the correct interface conditions between solid and fluid sub-cells.

(ii) Prove existence, uniqueness, and exponential decay away from the boundary for these correctors, including a characterization of their (possibly non-zero) asymptotic limits at infinity ("boundary-layer tails").

(iii) Determine the resulting first-order corrections to the homogenized macroscopic system: in particular, identify any modified effective boundary conditions (e.g. Fourier/Robin-type corrections) and/or additional terms in the effective equations that the boundary layer induces in the two cases.

(iv) Establish the corresponding optimal convergence rate of $u^\varepsilon$ to $u^0$ plus the constructed boundary-layer corrector, in suitable energy norms.
artifact.status_search_result: Boundary layers in periodic homogenization are well studied in scalar elliptic and elasticity settings (Allaire–Amar 1999; Gérard-Varet–Masmoudi), with established results on existence, exponential decay, boundary-layer tails, and Fourier-type effective boundary corrections. For coupled solid–fluid (poroelastic/Biot, Stokes-in-perforated-domain) systems, formal homogenization and partial rigorous results exist, but a complete characterization of boundary-layer correctors and optimal corrector estimates for both clamped and free-surface conditions in solid–fluid mixtures remains incomplete and is actively investigated.

status_evidence.title: Boundary layer tails in periodic homogenization
status_evidence.snippet: Boundary layers are highly oscillating near the boundary and decay exponentially fast in the interior; they yield a dispersive term and an effective Fourier boundary condition.
status_evidence.claim: Boundary-layer theory established for periodic homogenization with rigorous decay and effective Fourier-type corrections in the scalar/elliptic setting.

status_evidence.title: Homogenization and boundary layers (Gérard-Varet, Masmoudi)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies boundary layer correctors in periodic homogenization, including systems and non-aligned boundaries.
status_evidence.claim: General theory for boundary layers in homogenization of systems is developed but extensions to coupled mixtures are nontrivial.

status_evidence.title: Characterization of the mechanical behaviors of solid-fluid mixture by the homogenization method
status_evidence.snippet: Homogenization-based asymptotic expansions yield poroelasticity and viscoelasticity systems for solid-fluid mixtures.
status_evidence.claim: Effective macroscopic models for solid-fluid mixtures are derived formally; boundary-layer analysis is a known open/active issue.

status_evidence.title: Corrector estimates and homogenization errors
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on optimal corrector estimates including boundary-layer effects.
status_evidence.claim: Corrector/boundary-layer estimates remain an active area, with recent advances but no fully general theory for solid-fluid mixtures.
